fieldData.course-description: In collaboration with the Professional Security Knowledge Network (PSKN), Bow Valley College is offering Alberta Basic Security Training.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc:
In collaboration with the Professional Security Knowledge Network (PSKN), Bow Valley College is offering Alberta Basic Security Training.

This is a comprehensive training course for individuals seeking to enter this industry. It is designed to increase knowledge about the daily duties and responsibilities of a security professional and build the confidence needed to meet the challenges of the workplace.

This is an online course delivered in seven modules and is equivalent to 40 hours of classroom instruction. The course prepares you to write the provincial licensing exam.

Provincial Licensing Exam

The fee includes one sitting of the exam. You can complete the one hour exam at home, being supervised by a trained and approved proctor from eProctor Canada. If you are successful, you will receive your Licensing Exam Certificate from the Alberta Solicitor General’s Office by email within 3-4 business days.

To be eligible to apply for the Provincial Licensing Exam, you must:

  • be over 18 years old,
  • be eligible to work in Canada,
  • be fluent in English,
  • have no criminal record,
  • have no outstanding criminal charges, and
  • not be the subject of a criminal investigation.

To apply for your license, you must have your Licensing Exam Certificate. Visit the Alberta Security Department Website.

fieldData.course-description: This module focuses on the elements informing the development of a robust maintenance program.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc:
‍

Module 5 focuses on the elements informing the development of a robust maintenance program, which aims at physical assets performing safely, capably, reliably, and repeatedly to their desired performance in their given operating context. Introductory topics include failure definitions, the fundamentals of a maintenance program, and asset criticality analysis, followed by the main types of maintenance and their associated tasks. The second part of the course deals with processes and methodologies used to develop a maintenance program. This includes Reliability Centered Maintenance (RCM) and a detailed review of the seven questions, as well as a few other processes. The last part of the course covers the PMO method and additional tools to identify tactics. At the end of the course, participants will have a better understanding of what developing a maintenance program entails and an informed knowledge of the various maintenance processes and methods used in the industry.

‍

fieldData.course-description: Practical Nurse graduates, prepare to write your national exam with confidence.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc:
This course is offered online, synchronous.  You can prepare to write the Canadian Practical Nurse Registration (CPNRE) exam (available at the Bow Valley College Testing Centre) with confidence. You will review study and test-taking strategies, and write the CPNRE classroom Predictor Test.  Your instructor will review your exam results and help you to develop a personalized study plan as required.

The CPNRE Predictor Test is a two-hour online test, consisting of 85 multiple-choice questions matching the Blueprint for the Canadian Practical Nurse Registration Examination (CPNRE).  Once you have completed the CPNRE Predictor Test and submitted your answers, you will have access to your test results, in the form of a Performance Profile. The Performance Profile will be available to download and save in PDF format.

The Performance Profile provides the following:

  • Your score on the CPNRE Predictor Test
  • Your probability of passing the CPNRE
  • Your score in each of the competency categories, cognitive levels and client age categories tested by the CPNRE. This allows you to determine in which areas you need to focus your studying

‍

Additional Information

All course materials, including the CPNRE Predictor Test license are included in your course fee.  When you book your national exam through Pearson Vue, you can choose the Bow Valley College Testing Centre located in West Campus.

fieldData.course-description: The Practice of Commercial Real course equips aspiring professionals with the essential knowledge and skills for a successful career in commercial real estate.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc:
The Practice of Commercial Real Estate is designed for real estate professionals seeking to specialize in the commercial real estate sector, which is comprised of office, retail, industrial, recreational, multi-residential, and land development.

Building on the foundation presented in the Fundamentals of Real Estate course, this course explores the unique attributes of different commercial properties, the factors and analyses upon which real estate investment decisions are based, the fundamental concepts and processes involved in leasing commercial properties, key matters and issues that can impact commercial real estate professionals in their practice, common errors and omissions commercial real estate professionals commit, career considerations for new commercial real estate professionals, and each real estate professional’s role in Alberta’s self-regulated real estate industry.

Key topics include interpretation of commercial markets, investment property analysis, leasing principles, common errors and commission, professionalism, and the role of real estate professionals in Alberta’s real estate industry.

‍

Real Estate Licensing Eligibility:

Students wanting to become licensed in real estate in Alberta, must first meet the Real Estate Council of Alberta (RECA) eligibility requirements. Visit the RECA's Getting Licensed information page for more details.

  1. Complete the eligibility process with RECA.
  2. Once RECA approves your eligibility, enroll in he courses you wish to take at Bow Valley College. Please note that you will need to submit your REA eligibility approval confirmation to the college.
  3. Check your email for confirmation of your course registration.

‍

‍

Course Features:

Have you completed RELE9101 Fundamentals of Real Estate and your licensing exam and are ready for more? This course offers a detailed dive into the tools, competencies, and expertise needed to excel in Commercial Real Estate.

  • Pre-requisites: RELE9101 Fundamentals of Real Estate (or completion of the Fundamentals of Real Estate course at another institution). Verification will be required.
  • Course Delivery: Self-paced online study with access to an industry expert instructor.  
  • Course Schedule: Six months to complete the course. A recommended 15-week course is provided in the course outline.
  • Course length: 80-110 hours based on learners' existing knowledge, experience in the industry, and active engagement with student supports.
  • Completion Requirements: A minimum of 70% is required to pass the course.
  • Language of instruction: English
  • Accreditation: Officially recognized by RECA as an approved course.
  • Validity: 3 months to write RECA’s pre-licensing exam upon completing this course.

‍

RECA Licensing Exam:

Students must meet the RECA Eligibility requirements and successfully pass this course. Students will need to successfully complete RECA examination to become licensed.

  • Exam: Administered by RECA. See RECA’s Exam Guide to learn more.
  • Exam Length: 3 hours
  • Exam attempts: 2

This comprehensive course highlights the multifaceted nature of property management, emphasizing the need for proficiency in areas like leasing strategies, marketing tactics, financial acumen, and fundamental property valuation skills. Learners examine the property manager’s role and explore the tools, competencies, and legal frameworks that impact the effective management of diverse property portfolios. The course is designed to meet the dynamic needs of property managers, tenants, and landlords in contemporary markets.

Key topics also covered include leasing best practices, tenant selection criteria, pertinent legislative considerations, efficient property operations, residential tenancy management, and trust accounting principles. By the end of this course, learners will be well-prepared for a career in property management and to successfully complete the RECA licensing exam.
